title: King Oliver as a reluctant front man, his cataract and jealousy
summary: Oliver stayed behind the band because of a cataract on his eye and was touchy about women in the band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Anybody else that he ever commented on?
Yeah. What's this cat's name used to play with King in Chicago?
What did he play? What instrument?
He played trumpet. He was in one of them big bands King had. I heard you call his name in there one time.
Oh, I did call his name. Well, what did he have to say about him? Maybe that will help you.
He said he was a good trumpet player. King said he used to... See, you'd take... Back in those days,

there was just certain musicians that could play a show -- Black musicians that could play a show. King said they had him play in the club, but he led the band, took care of the band playing the show. Because King wasn't no kind of a front man. No, he wasn't no front man. He would never get up in front of the band. Never would. Looked like he liked to stay here somewhat. I know why he did it. It was on account of his eye. See, he had a big cataract on his eye, and it was very noticeable.
So he couldn't see out of that eye?

No. But I mean, he was conscious of it. You know what I mean? He always figured that people... He figured that eye kind of weighed him down to a certain extent. He would get women, pick up on some chick sometimes, and they probably liked some of the guys in the band -- they were younger women, you know what I mean? They wouldn't think too much about King -- only his money. He would say, "Well, I know I'm an ugly son-of-a-bitch, but I don't want nobody fuckin' with my woman." Like, a lot of the chicks would come in... One chick was with the band, she went wild about Red -- Red Elkins. Things like that, you know. He was kind of...
